samples.summary: Deferred release runs mid-press, so the "popup still open" guard is evaluated before a click-opened popup exists
samples.evidence: `onFocusIn` schedules `setTimeout(..., 0)`; `focusin` for a mouse click fires on **mousedown**, not on `click`. For any real (human) press — tens to hundreds of ms between mousedown and mouseup — the timeout fires while the button is still held down, i.e. before the `click` that actually opens a Radix `Popover` (PopoverTrigger opens on `onClick`). At that moment `hasOpenPopup(trigger)` is false (`data-state="closed"`, `aria-expanded="false"`), so the trigger is blurred during the press and the guard that exists to keep a trigger focused while its popup is open never applies to click-opening triggers. Today the consequence is benign only because every slides picker is `<Popover modal>` (shape-controls.tsx:219, border-picker.tsx:110, text-element-controls.tsx:118, table-controls.tsx:286) and re-focuses its own content; a non-modal popover added later would be blurred and Radix's `onFocusOutside` would dismiss it. The co-located tests cannot catch this because `userEvent.click` has no press delay, so in jsdom the timeout always lands after `click`.

samples.summary: `keyboardNavigating` latches on any Tab keydown and is only cleared by a pointerdown, so several close paths leave the toolbar button focused (#882 persists)
samples.evidence: `onKeyDown` sets `keyboardNavigating = true` for every `Tab` keydown anywhere in the document — including Tab consumed as a *canvas* shortcut (the slides Tab-cycle rule; see the comment at packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:877 and the Tab rules in `buildKeyRules`) and Tab pressed inside a modal Radix menu, where focus is trapped and Tab does not move focus out at all. The flag is cleared only by `onPointerDown`. Consequently, after e.g. a mouse-opened menu where the user then presses Tab (trapped, flag latches) and activates an item with Enter, Radix returns focus to the toolbar trigger and the release is skipped: `isEditableTarget()` stays engaged and arrow keys / Delete / z-order shortcuts remain dead until the user clicks something. Same for any keyboard-driven dialog/menu close that returns focus into the toolbar with no intervening pointerdown.

samples.summary: Release is purely `focusin`-driven, so a close path that leaves focus unchanged on an already-focused toolbar button never releases
samples.evidence: The only trigger for a release is a `focusin` whose target is inside `[data-canvas-toolbar]`. If a popup closes while its trigger is already `document.activeElement` (Radix calling `trigger.focus()` on the already-active element dispatches no focus event), no release is ever scheduled and the button keeps the keyboard — exactly the #882 state. That cannot happen for the current slides pickers only because they are all `modal` and move focus into their content on open; the hook has no fallback (e.g. checking `document.activeElement` on the closing `data-state` transition or on a document-level `pointerdown`/keydown) for a non-modal popup, an `onOpenAutoFocus`-prevented content, or a control focused before the toolbar mounted.
searchedFor: grep for `<Popover`/`<DropdownMenu`/`modal` under packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar (all popovers are `modal`)
grep for onOpenAutoFocus / onCloseAutoFocus in slides (table-picker.tsx:80 redirects focus into portalled content)
read menu-focus.ts to check the existing `useMenuCloseHandlers` close path

samples.summary: `hasOpenPopup`'s `data-state==="open"` check is defeated by triggers that hand-set `data-state`; the guard survives only via `aria-expanded`
samples.evidence: `hasOpenPopup()` (toolbar-focus-release.ts:54) treats `data-state="open"` as "popup open", but slides toolbar triggers deliberately override that attribute for pressed styling: `data-state={activeKind !== null ? "on" : "off"}` on the `DropdownMenuTrigger asChild` child in shape-picker.tsx:109 and line-picker.tsx:199. Radix `Slot` gives child props precedence, so while those menus are OPEN the element reports `data-state="on"`/`"off"`, and only Radix's own `aria-expanded="true"` keeps the hook from blurring an open picker's trigger. Any toolbar trigger that overrides `data-state` and is not a Radix trigger emitting `aria-expanded` (or any picker whose trigger is a plain controlled `<button>`) would be blurred while its popup is open.
searchedFor: read shape-picker.tsx trigger composition (TooltipTrigger asChild > DropdownMenuTrigger asChild > button)

finding.summary: `pointerDriven` gate skips the most common dismissal path (click outside onto the canvas), where Radix *modal* Popovers force focus back onto the toolbar trigger — so issue #882 still reproduces there
finding.evidence: `onFocusIn` bails out unless the last `pointerdown` landed inside the toolbar or a popup (`isPointerDrivenTarget`, lines 80-87). Every slides colour/border picker is a **modal** Popover (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/shape-controls.tsx:219`, `text-element-controls.tsx:118`, `table-controls.tsx:286`, `border-picker.tsx:110`). Radix's `PopoverContentModal` default `onCloseAutoFocus` unconditionally does `context.triggerRef.current?.focus()` (only right-click-outside is exempt), and `useMenuCloseHandlers.onCloseAutoFocus` (`menu-focus.ts:52-57`) only `preventDefault()`s when a swatch was clicked. So: open Fill ▾, dismiss it by clicking the canvas → pointerdown target is outside the toolbar → `pointerDriven = false` → the trigger `<button>` ends up focused and the hook deliberately does nothing. `isEditableTarget` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:882) then keeps eating every shortcut, i.e. the exact bug the change claims to close. Same hole when the user Tabs inside an open picker (Tab clears the flag) and then closes it. Note `menu-focus.ts:26-29` asserts outside-click 'falls through to Radix's default focus-to-trigger, then the natural click target / body keep focus', which is not what modal Popover does.

verdict.reason: The finding describes a `pointerDriven` / `isPointerDrivenTarget` gate that requires the last pointerdown to land inside the toolbar or a popup. No such variable or function exists anywhere in the repo (grep for `pointerDriven|isPointerDrivenTarget` returns zero matches). The actual gate is the inverse: `keyboardNavigating` is set true ONLY by a Tab keydown (toolbar-focus-release.ts:100) and cleared by ANY pointerdown regardless of target (:95-97); `onFocusIn` bails only when `keyboardNavigating` is true (:104). So clicking the canvas to dismiss a modal Popover clears the flag, and the trigger focus that Radix's `onCloseAutoFocus` restores IS released (:116-118, with `hasOpenPopup` false once the popup has closed, :54-59/:72). The module comment at :84-91 explicitly rejects the "pointerdown must land inside the toolbar" design the finding attributes to it, and a regression test pins the exact claimed-broken path (test file :137-149: pointerdown on canvas, then trigger.focus(), asserting focus released). The secondary Tab-inside-picker remark describes the hook's documented and tested keyboard-user carve-out, not the asserted hole.
